rationale: The same scene in the same order after the descent from the mountain: a father whose son the disciples could not help, Jesus' cry "How long must I put up with you?" (Matthew 17:17; Mark 9:19, BSB), the rebuke of the spirit, and the disciples' private question "Why couldn't we drive it out?" (Matthew 17:19; Mark 9:28). Parallel/strong rather than explicit, following conn-matt16-sign-mark8, because neither Gospel names the other and the differences are real and checkable in the BSB. Matthew's father says his son "has seizures" (17:15), where Mark's speaks of "a spirit that makes him mute" (Mark 9:17). Only Mark has the exchange in which the father cries, "I do believe; help my unbelief!" (9:24). Matthew alone answers the disciples with "Because you have so little faith" and the mustard-seed saying (17:20); Mark's answer is "This kind cannot come out, except by prayer" (9:29), where the Byzantine and Textus Receptus editions add "and fasting." Matthew 17:21, which this app's BSB leaves empty, is the verse whose place in Matthew the manuscripts dispute; the lesson reports that question, and this row does not depend on it.
